strategyPosture: Stay selective and staged. Credit is loose (SLOOS 0%, HY OAS 3.03%) and the index is near its high, so there is no confirmed rollover to de-risk against — but a 5.60% 30-year and rotating leadership argue for owning the verified dislocations (AVGO-grade fundamentals at sentiment prices) rather than chasing the nuclear unwind or paying up at the index level.

themes.counterRead: Historically this combination — index near highs, leadership diverging, credit loose — resolves as rotation rather than a confirmed broad top. But the divergence is real: if the gap widens while credit starts confirming, the read flips. Position for churn in leadership, not for index collapse.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 10.26% below their 52-week highs versus SPY at 1.1% — a 9.16-point divergence gap. TSLA is the weakest Mag7 name at 25.5% off its high; AAPL the strongest at 1.7%. Critically, bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress zone) and HY OAS sits at 3.03% — credit is not confirming a rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY is 1.1% off its 52-week high — so the market read is that nothing is wrong. Underneath, the leadership that carried the index is being rotated out of, and today QQQ fell 1.62% against SPY's 0.71% with VIX up 5.11% to 15.85.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap: narrowing from 9.16 pts means rotation healing; widening past ~12 pts with HY OAS above 3.50% means rollover risk.

themes.counterRead: The speculative leg (SMR, OKLO) has no fundamental anchor in the current data — those declines are sentiment-driven and can extend. BWXT is the opposite shape: a real business being sold with the theme. Lumping them together is the error; the unwind is narrative-ahead for the story stocks and data-ahead for the quality name.
themes.dataAnchor: The month's laggards are dominated by nuclear: SMR −33.35% in one month (−6.06% today), OKLO −20.26% (−7.81% today), URA −18.65%, CCJ −14.21%. Holding VST fell 6.34% today. But the complex is not homogeneous — BWXT is 41.1% below its high while revenue grows 18.3% YoY with positive FCF, a fundamentals/price divergence the screen scores 77 (Tier B).
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power Unwind
themes.narrative: The AI-power complex is being unwound as a crowded narrative trade: the market is treating every nuclear name as the same story stock and selling the complex together.
themes.watchFor: SMR/OKLO posting two consecutive positive weeks after −33%/−20% months would mark capitulation ending; BWXT reclaiming a positive 1-month trend on its revenue base is the quality tell.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals and price are moving in opposite directions — that is the definition of the setup, but it is not a timing signal by itself. A 5.60% 30-year caps the multiple the market will pay for even this growth, so the discount can persist until the rate path or the next print forces a re-rate.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is the screen's top conviction name (score 81, Tier A): revenue growing 55% YoY, gross margin 67.8%, free cash flow $26.9B at a 42.1% FCF margin — while the stock sits at $361.10, 27.1% below its 52-week high, RSI 49.8. The semi-equipment layer underneath confirms recovery rather than rollover: AMAT +9.2% and KLAC +7.7% one-month trends on multiple-compression (not fundamental) decline tags, CLS revenue +28.5%, VRT revenue +27.7%.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Quality at a Discount
themes.narrative: The tape is pricing Broadcom like a cyclical that already peaked — sold off with the AI complex on a sentiment-driven decline signal despite no fundamental break in the data.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding above its recent range low while revenue growth stays near +55% at the next print; a revenue deceleration would close the fundamentals-ahead-of-price gap from the wrong side.

themes.counterRead: Tight credit plus a steep curve is a multiple-compression regime, not a recession signal — it punishes long-duration cash flows (small caps, unprofitable growth) while cash-generative quality holds up. The risk is a hot CPI on Oct 14 pushing the 30-year through 5.60% and turning compression into a broader de-rating.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve has bear-steepened: DGS2 4.79%, DGS10 5.22%, DGS30 5.60%, 2s10s +0.43, real 10-year 2.86%, breakeven 2.36%. HY OAS at 3.03% says credit disagrees with the stress story. The casualty is duration-sensitive breadth: IWM is −4.6% over one month and −5.52% over three while SPY is +1.22%/+3.53%. Fed funds (DFF) sit at 3.88% with FOMC decisions on Oct 27–28 and Dec 8–9 ahead.
themes.label: The Long End Is the Pressure Point
themes.narrative: The market's anxiety is inflation and duration — futures headlines flag 'inflation jitters' into the September CPI — not credit or growth collapse.
themes.watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14: DGS30 holding below 5.60% keeps the compression contained; a push through 5.75% with HY OAS widening past 3.50% changes the regime.

themes.counterRead: Depth of drawdown is not evidence of value — some of these declines are the market correctly repricing slower futures, and the screen does not separate those from sentiment overshoot. This is a research queue, not a buy list: each name needs its thesis verified before sizing, exactly as the posture flag in the data states.
themes.dataAnchor: The dislocation screen flags FULL_SIGNAL sentiment-driven declines in names whose revenue still grows: NOW is 28.7% below its high with revenue +23.1% YoY (RSI 53.8); HUBS is 54.1% below its high; TTD 77.7% below. The pullback posture in the data is RESEARCH_SCREENED — every candidate passed the 5-gate screen, but the screen verifies dislocation, not thesis.
themes.label: Dislocated Quality Growth
themes.narrative: A broad set of former growth leaders has been written off as broken — software and platform names sit 25–75% below their highs and the market is pricing them as structurally impaired.
themes.watchFor: Names from this screen printing revenue re-acceleration on their next reports while holding above post-decline bases; continued estimate cuts on the same names would confirm the impairment read instead.

watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14 — DGS30 (now 5.60%) holding below 5.60% vs pushing through 5.75%
Mag7-vs-SPY 52-week-high divergence gap narrowing from 9.16 pts (rotation healing) or widening past ~12 pts (rollover risk)
HY OAS staying at or below ~3.25% (credit calm) vs breaking above 3.50% (credit confirming stress)
AVGO holding its recent range while revenue growth prints near +55% YoY — the data-ahead test case
SMR/OKLO two consecutive positive weeks after −33%/−20% months — capitulation signal for the nuclear complex
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds on the rate path into September CPI (Oct 14) and the Oct 27–28 FOMC: a soft print relieves the long end and re-rates the dislocated quality growth first; a hot print extends multiple compression, with IWM (−5.52% over three months) as the pressure gauge.
